name: Bildad
overview: Bildad is a male figure identified as the Shuhite and a friend of Job, as noted in Job 2:11. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture. Beyond his role as a friend to Job, no additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Bildad means 'Bel has loved,' reflecting a proper name of ancient origin. This meaning is provided in the Hebrew context as recorded in Job 2:11. There are no additional titles or names associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Bildad beyond his designation as a friend of Job. There are no listed relatives or other connections mentioned.
scriptureSignificance: Bildad's significance lies in his role as one of Job's friends who appears during Job's trials, specifically identified as the Shuhite. His presence in the narrative contributes to the exploration of suffering and divine justice. Though limited information is given, his interaction with Job is part of the broader theological discourse in the book of Job.
